cards.title: Iran peace deadline arrives with Hormuz reopening still unresolved
cards.summary: AP reported Monday that the 60-day deadline for a U.S.-Iran peace deal arrived without a visible compromise on reopening the Strait of Hormuz or beginning detailed nuclear talks.
detail: Associated Press reported on Aug. 17 that the 60-day deadline set by the June Versailles agreement had arrived while the two sides remained further apart. Talks have focused on reopening the Strait of Hormuz and lifting the U.S. blockade, but AP reported no sign of a compromise or detailed nuclear negotiations.

The unresolved waterway question matters beyond diplomacy: Hormuz carried about a fifth of the world’s traded oil and gas before the war, so navigation, insurance, and energy-price risk remain linked to the talks. The UAE’s earlier attribution of tanker attacks to Iran is still an attributed claim, not a completed independent finding.

The next evidence is concrete movement on access through the strait, the blockade, and a verifiable negotiating channel. Until those appear, the deadline is a marker of stalled diplomacy rather than proof of a settled end-state.
